title: USP Embedded Scheduling Protocol (ESP) Messages
description: Canonical wire schemas for the Embedded Scheduling Protocol defined in specification.md Section 9.5. ESP carries JSON-RPC 2.0 messages over a MessageChannel (web) or injected globals (native), between a host application and an embedded business scheduling UI. Section 9.5.3 requires every ESP message to be validated against its schema before processing; these $defs are the artifact that requirement refers to. ESP frames are neither HTTP responses nor USP transport-binding calls, so ESP failures use the esp.error frame codes defined here rather than the Section 9.4 error families. Every message shares the same JSON-RPC 2.0 framing: jsonrpc is exactly "2.0", method is one of the twelve registered esp.* names, params carries the message-specific payload, and id is present only on frames that expect a correlated reply.

Delegation.title: Delegation
Delegation.description: A step the host can perform on the business's behalf. slot_selection: host renders the time slot picker. party_details: host supplies buyer and optional recipient information. payment: host acquires the payment credential. See specification.md Section 9.5.2.

EspParticipant.title: EspParticipant
EspParticipant.description: A buyer or recipient as carried over ESP. Deliberately a subset of booking.json Buyer: an embedded UI negotiates identity progressively, so no field is required at the envelope level and the business validates completeness for its own flow.

EspReady.title: esp.ready
EspReady.description: Business to Host. The embedded UI has loaded and is ready. Declares which delegations the business supports.

delegations.description: Delegations the business is willing to hand to the host. MAY be empty, meaning the business handles every step itself.

service_id.description: The service the embedded UI was opened for, when the host addressed a specific service.

version.description: USP protocol version the embedded UI implements.

EspStart.title: esp.start
EspStart.description: Host to Business. Starts the scheduling flow and accepts a subset of the offered delegations. A delegation not listed in accepted_delegations is handled by the business internally.

recipient.description: The person receiving the service when that is not the buyer.

preferences.description: Non-binding hints to pre-filter what the embedded UI shows.

accepted_delegations.description: MUST be a subset of the delegations array from esp.ready. A host MUST NOT accept a delegation the business did not offer.

EspSlotSelectionRequest.title: esp.slot_selection.request
EspSlotSelectionRequest.description: Business to Host. Asks the host to render its own slot picker. Sent only when slot_selection is an accepted delegation.

slots.description: Candidate slots for the host to render. When absent, the host queries availability itself.

duration.description: ISO 8601 duration of the booking being scheduled.

EspSlotSelectionResponse.title: esp.slot_selection.response
EspSlotSelectionResponse.description: Host to Business. Returns the slot the user selected.

slot.description: The selected slot. MUST be one the business can still honour; the business revalidates availability regardless.

resources.description: Resources bound to the selected slot, when the host offered a resource choice.

EspPartyDetailsRequest.title: esp.party_details.request
EspPartyDetailsRequest.description: Business to Host. Asks the host to supply participant details. Sent only when party_details is an accepted delegation.

required_fields.description: Field names the business needs before it can proceed (e.g. first_name, email, phone_number).

party_size.description: Number of participants the business expects details for.

EspPartyDetailsResponse.title: esp.party_details.response
EspPartyDetailsResponse.description: Host to Business. Returns participant information.

EspPaymentCredentialRequest.title: esp.payment.credential_request
EspPaymentCredentialRequest.description: Business to Host. Asks the host to acquire a payment credential for the stated amount. Sent only when payment is an accepted delegation.

amount.description: Amount to authorize, in minor currency units.

booking_id.description: The pending booking the payment applies to, when the business has already created one.

accepted_handlers.description: Reverse-domain payment handler identifiers the business accepts. The host MUST return a credential for one of these.

EspPaymentCredentialResponse.title: esp.payment.credential_response
EspPaymentCredentialResponse.description: Host to Business. Returns the acquired payment credential. The credential is opaque to USP: its shape is defined by the payment handler specification in use.

handler_id.description: The payment handler that issued the credential. MUST be one of accepted_handlers when that array was supplied.

credential.description: Handler-defined credential payload. USP does not constrain its members, and implementations MUST NOT log it.

EspComplete.title: esp.complete
EspComplete.description: Business to Host. Terminal success frame: the booking reached its final state for this session.

status.description: Terminal booking status for this ESP session. canceled is the frame sent in response to esp.cancel when the business chooses to complete rather than error.

booking.description: Full booking object, when the business returns it inline.

EspErrorCode.title: EspErrorCode
EspErrorCode.description: Well-known esp.error codes. These are ESP frame codes, a family distinct from the Section 9.4 business outcome codes and protocol errors: an ESP frame is neither an HTTP response nor a JSON-RPC transport error. Implementations MAY send other codes, which hosts MUST treat as unrecoverable unless recoverable says otherwise.

EspError.title: esp.error
EspError.description: Business to Host. An error occurred during a delegation step.

recoverable.description: Whether the host may retry the step. Required, because a host cannot otherwise tell a declined card from a dead session.

EspCancel.title: esp.cancel
EspCancel.description: Host to Business. Cancels the in-progress flow. The business MUST release any held slots and reply with esp.error code canceled, or esp.complete with status canceled.

reason.description: Optional host-supplied reason, for diagnostics only.

EspTimeout.title: esp.timeout
EspTimeout.description: Business to Host. The session expired with no messages exchanged inside the timeout window. Pending holds are released and partial booking state is discarded.

timeout_seconds.description: The window that elapsed. Default is 1800 (30 minutes).

EspMessage.title: EspMessage
EspMessage.description: Any ESP message. Validators dispatch on the method const. Section 9.5.3 requires both peers to validate an incoming frame against this schema before acting on it.
